title: Good little app but my god
text:
app designers really need to chill the f out with these subscription prices. 

you used to purchase an app once, and be done with it.  this isn’t like netflix where I can explore an ever-expanding platform of entertainment.

when you bought a program for your PC, you bought it once and outright owned it. 

justifying nearly £30 to have the app for only a YEAR before having to repay that price again is ludicrous.  

These things should be a ONE TIME payment and that’s IT

And even then, nearly £30 is way way too much to ask people to pay. 

In the free version: this works well, but you can only have 2 routines going. you are very limited on the icons you can use, as many of them only come with a subscription.  

Paying for that subscription, like it is with most other apps that slap such a huge fee on an app that… doesn’t really do that much ????, is allowing yourself to be robbed. 

Stardew Valley, with endless gameplay, costs less than this to buy outright.  Why on earth anyone thinks these prices are reasonable is beyond me

title: Teilweise gut, teilweise naja
text:
Viele Funktionen in der App sind sinnvoll, generell funktioniert das Konzept für mich auch ganz gut.

Gleichzeitig scheint die App aber auch nicht sehr kompetent entwickelt worden zu sein. Es gibt immer mal wieder mal nen Absturz, Übersetzungen sind mal deutsch, mal niederländisch, mal englisch und insgesamt schlecht. Das Layout ist manchmal nicht ganz zu Ende gedacht und etwas zu verschwenderisch mit dem Platz. Und Synchronisierung zwischen den Geräten ist nur so naja. Manchmal verändern sich Routinen durch Bugs, was sehr nervig ist. Und auf dem iPad skaliert die ganze App nicht vernünftig.

Ich glaube die App muss grundlegend mal neu geschrieben werden, weil es so schon seit Monaten ist.

title: Please make this a one-time purchase instead of a subscription!
text:
This would be a five-star review except that I will probably always be stuck using the free version (which limits you to two routines) because I am unwilling to pay a monthly fee for something that should be a one-time purchase.

This app has been a game-changer for my ADHD, hugely helpful for getting me out the door to work mostly on time in the morning and helping me wind down for bedtime in a timely manner. I took a year off from using Routinery in 2023 because I had a baby and wasn’t working, and my routines kept changing as my baby grew. Now, in 2024, I’m going back to work (and also now having to get my daughter off to daycare!) so I’m back! I was disappointed to discover that, in addition to limiting the user to two routines, the free version now apparently has ads??? I would love to make a one-time purchase in order to unlock the premium features of this app, but really, really don’t want to pay $27 per year (or $95 per year at full price!)

title: Need to rely on my phone less to use Routinery
text:
This app has been extremely helpful in keeping me on track during my morning/evening routines. I also prefer to use it primarily on my Apple Watch instead of my iPhone. But in the morning, especially, I really don’t like having to pull up the app on my phone first in order to use it on my watch. It kind of defeats the purpose of keeping the first couple hours of my morning phone-free. 

I would love it if, in a future update, you could work in the ability to start the routine timers in the watch app without having to open the phone app first. And if that isn’t feasible - are there any plans to introduce a Lock Screen widget in a future update? That could at least help avoid the risk of getting distracted and not opening Routinery when I unlock my phone.

title: The app I have needed for so long
text:
Since I was young I have always built little written-down morning and evening routines for myself, knowing it would put me on track to have the best day possible, stay productive, and build great habits. The issue I always ran into was my inability to stay motivated and focused on those little to-do’s. I’d always lose track and constantly felt disheartened thinking I just lacked discipline.

Turns out my ADHD brain just needed a little help! This app is truly perfect—if I could’ve created the ideal app for me that did everything I wanted it to do when it comes to building and applying daily routines, it would be this app down to every detail! 

It’s so simple yet incredibly effective and genuinely a great help. 

A biggggg “thank you” to the creators of this app!

title: Excellent application
text: J’aurais mit 4 étoiles mais je me dois d’être le plus précis possible quant a mon feedback. L’appli est super bien pensée et pour moi qui suis TDAH et souhaite être lus organisé est meilleure de 1% chaque jours, c’est super ! Pleins de fonctionnalités que je trouve super interessantes, je reviendrais mettre a jour le commentaire afin d’apporter plus de précision sur ça et une ou deux suggestions. Bien partit pour mettre 5 étoiles néanmoins j’ai rencontré un bug ajd, ma première tache de la journée sensée être effectuée depuis ce matin 5h30, s’est remise sur mon écran de verrouillage et m’affiche +8h comme si je ne l’avais pas validée depuis ce laps de temps. Quand je clique pour la valider, il valide en réalité la tache qui est actuellement sous décompte, car quand j’ouvre l’application, ce n’est pas ma première tache du matin qui s’affiche mais bien la tache du moment comme si tout fonctionnait bien, je penses que le bug se situe au niveau du Widget écran verrouillé, je penses tout de même que le bug intervient lorsque mon mode Travail (concentration) se désactive et laisse place a un autre mode, si ce bug est résolu, je met 5 étoiles et paye pour avoir l’accès complet, car cette appli est incroyable 💪🏾 HANMA PROJECT 1% BETTER EVERYDAY

text: Since the 3.22.0 update I can't rearrange the tasks in either of my routines. At this point the screen freezes for a second, and then the task I just moved unsuccessfully suddenly teleports to another random place in the list all by itself. This happens the same way in the regular list view, in the actual edit mode, and on the change order screen while the routine is in progress. I rearrange my routines often (thanks ADHD!) so this bug has almost completely stopped me using the app for over a month where I previously had a streak of well over a year. title: Amazing app for staying present, especially with ADHD
text: Ever since I started using this app, I feel so regulated and content. The timers help me focus on one task at a time and not get sidetracked, so I’m able to feel calmer and less overwhelmed by everything there is to do. I know that the app will tell me what to do next, so I don’t need to keep reminding myself of all the things I need to do. I never have to dig into my brain to make sure I remembered to do everything (and make sure I do everything in the right order, stay on track, remember what to do next, etc.). At first I thought the timers would stress me out, but they actually just force me to surrender and do the task at hand — and it gives me a sense of pride when I finish something early/on time. When I get ready for the day and unwind from the day, I can let go of all my thoughts, worries, and tension, and just be. This calmness and stability carries over to the rest of my day and to my night of sleep. Thank you for this beautiful app and I highly recommend to anyone <3

title: Great features but needs improvements to be worth the money.
text:
Pros:
-screen stays on while app is open, with a countdown for each activity
-notification sounds at 1 min before activity ends, and at end (you can change this, and decide whether to automatically or manually switch tasks)
-voice that tells you to switch activities (helpful if you can’t be looking at the screen at all times)
 -ability to skip an activity for the day (during or before routine starts)

Other routine apps have been missing these features, which are essential for this to be effective for me.

However… cons:
-app sends you banner notifications between activities even when app is open and not in the background
-primary issue—you can only do a routine once per day, and you cannot adjust a routine you’re going to do tomorrow if you have already done it today. Especially in free version this is extremely frustrating as I need to change my routine depending on the day and how much time I have.
-secondary issue—sound is a bit of a mess. You can adjust with phone volume, but the app volume will randomly shoot way up and start shouting at you, which in addition to scaring me can also be heard by the neighboring apt.
-the voice sometimes calls out the wrong activity
-no connection to a calendar/schedule as some other apps have, this is helpful

 Overall, I’d like more than just the 2 free routines, but can’t justify that price without some changes being made to these issues—ESPECIALLY since you have to pay that price on a recurring basis!

title: Not a lot of bells & whistles for the price
text:
I’m updating my review here, because I’ve figured out all of the issues that I was having. The main issue with the text to speech can be turned off only while the routine is running. In day view, it’s grey and difficult to see, but it is there and it fixed my problem. I use this app everyday now, and it helps me focus on what’s important, so I do recommend it. The syncing is working great now, and the lagging only seemed to occur when I created my routines. So, I’m changing my review from 4 to 5 stars.

Old review:
Unlike many who have complained, I actually did subscribe to the annual subscription, and I get that the goal here is simplicity. But, simple design does not mean less features / functionality. The huge disappointment for me is that you can’t turn off the text-to-speech when a task runs over! I listen to audiobooks during my morning routine and I guess I’m going to have to run this on my iPad in the bathroom while my phone plays my audio, because there is no way to keep it from interrupting. If I had realized this before subscribing, I would not have subscribed. But, there aren’t really any other apps like this. In the past, I used apps like Seconds and MyIntervals, which are for creating workouts. They have way more options within each routine, and I don’t care about summaries or tracking overall progress. I do not have ADHD, nor am I neurodivergent - I just like to be organized. I do have depression and productivity apps help motivate me and keep me focused, so I do rely on them. I turned off the chatbot, which was annoying, and I’m glad that option was available, but there need to be more ways to customize. And, I agree that that the lag times are perplexing. When scrolling, it often freezes and you have to wait for it to “think”. I turned off all the automatic switches from one task to the next (took forever to do because of lag), hoping it would stop talking, but with no luck. It literally announces that the last task has ended automatically, in full, and that the next task has started, in full. Then, it keep nagging every minute over or so, too, even if I pause the routine! I have all routines set to silent with no automatic tasks and I cannot believe the text-to-speech is still so disruptive. I don’t even want it to beep - I just want to check the task when I’m done. I guess I can go make all the tasks way longer so I always complete the task within the timeframe, but I kind of wanted something with close to accurate times to push me - that was the point. Then, I guess I can just stop the routine if I need to stop to do something else for a few minutes, but how inconvenient, and who knows if it’s going to work properly, like save my previous tasks. It seems like whoever made this had a particular goal or vision , which is good, but the code and technical design needs work. I will say that it’s pretty reliable if the app gets closed or exited or anything, about keeping the time going. Any edits to routines get synced well to iCloud, but it doesn’t always sync daily progress between devices.

title: Changed my life the first day!!
text: I cannot say enough good things about this app!! I cannot believe this is all I’ve needed my entire life!! I normally live In a constant time warp! I would wake up at 8:30am sit down to drink my tea and then while still drinking tea I’d look at the clock and it’d be 3:00!! Normally I would spend my day planning my day but not end up with any time left to actually do anything I planned lol! I was always running late and never felt like I had enough time for anything! I didn’t even realized how distracted I was! I’d go to start laundry but then notice the bathroom needs to be cleaned so I’d start that and then notice the floors need to be swept so I’d jump to that and I’d try doing a million things at once stressing about time for all the other things and now I can just focus on one thing at a time because I know that everything is in my routine so I’ll get to those things at their time and don’t need to worry! I feel so at peace and so at ease now! I even schedule in stretching and meditation which I always tricked myself into thinking I didn’t have time for! At the end of my day i feel so energized and accomplished and I’m shocked that it’s so easy to keep up on all the chores and to prioritize self care at the same time! I never have laundry or dishes sitting for days… and I get everything done so fast and then I have so much free time and can actually enjoy it! I usually just felt super busy all day but would somehow not get anything done! I’m so thrilled that it’s only $2/ month to feel like I normal human! 😂

title: This app changed my life🌟🤩💕
text:
I am a school student trying to make the most of my teenage years. 🌅👯‍♀️✨ Although I have been doing terribly at this goal. 😩When I get home from school I find myself ruminating about what I said to people that day. I think about what I could of said that was better or if I said something stupid and they will leave me and I will be lonely again. I soon doom-scroll on my phone trying to distract myself📱. Even if I notice what I’m doing I feel like it is too late to do anything productive. I end up doing nothing till dinner.  When I go to bed I hate myself so much that I can’t sleep 🛌.

The cycle continued till I found your wonderful app🍃🌳🍃✨.  When I get home I made a shortcut that starts a routine, when I arrive home 🏠. I do yoga, meditation and journaling. I do homework after wards and focus perfectly. 
Since then I have gotten ‘A’s on every assessment I’ve been assigned! 🌟 I am so proud of my self. Then I do hobbies such as basketball, drawing and crocheting.🧶 I feel so much happier, more energetic, full-filled and more positive in every aspect of my life. This app saved me from so many bad days and sleepless nights. I can’t thank you all enough!🌸🌟✨Bug fixes are needed though!🐞🐜🐛. When I tap on my profile to type my name it takes me out of app. This is very frustrating and I would really appreciate it if this was fixed.

This is random but my sister always judges me for using this app and says it is brain washing. So sometimes i stop using it because I’m scared of being judged. Is it weird to use an app like this? 

Ps I love the plant icon as the first iron that appears. Plants symbolise growth which I find very powerful and encouraging🤩🍃🌳🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🌳
 
Once again, thank you so much for creating this spectacular app😊💫🤩✨✨✨ you are doing great in your updates. It is improving so much!🌸 I wish you all the best😃. Love from Australia 🇦🇺💕💕💕💕💕

text:

title: Must Pay for Full Usability
text:
I am looking for a habit-tracking app that is easy to use, doesn't require a subscription, and doesn't force you to watch advertisements.

Unfortunately, this application requires about $4/month. Some of the features that are locked for only subscribed users are custom reminder sounds, an ad-free experience, and satisfaction notes (recording your feelings). 

I like that this application asked me about my demographics and preferences so it could tailor the routine. I also liked that once the routine was created, I was able to adjust things like the time associated with the task. It is nice that the routine starts off with a quick breathing exercise. This application is ultimately not for me because I’m looking for something where I can actually analyze my data and discover patterns, which won’t be possible without paying.

title: Seems great, what's with the battery drain?
text:
Like the app a lot, I am a premium user. Very useful for establishing habits.

But if I leave Routinery on my iPad Pro m1, it will drain the entire full battery in a matter of a couple of hours! There is no sound playing, it's just the basic screen.

iOS reports Routinery as using over 90% of my battery each day. Something is up.

My other issue: you cannot sync routines between devices when they're running! I will open my phone to continue a routine I'm running, and it will not show any progress unless I stop the routine on the other device, then I can continue.

These two things are almost dealbreakers for an otherwise great app, especially how the second one makes the first worst, since I can't swap between devices to save my poor battery.

title: ADHDのライフライン
text:
これまでも様々なルーティンタイマー的なものを試してきましたが、ほんの些細なことにつまずいて挫折していました。

このアプリは一つひとつのルーティンに対する設定を細かく決められるので、この後は自動で次に、この後は止まってほしい、など自分仕様にアレンジできて、つまずきポイントを取り除いていけます。

今も定着まではいけていないので自分仕様に育ててつつ、タイムボクシングと組み合わせて謎に意識が飛ぶ数時間を無くしていきたいと思います。

ルーティンタイマーとしては申し分ない、完成形と言えるのではないかと。ADHD持ちにとっては生活を成り立たせるためのライフラインです。開発してくださり、ありがとうございます♩
author: Torajiro^_^

title: No More Getting Sidetracked
text:
My night routine was always just way too long. I would waste time on unnecessary things and forget things I meant to do. This app helps structure my evenings to fit in everything I need and nothing I don’t. To TRULY show how perfect this app is: I have flossed everyday for a month! What a win ;)

Also, the timer shows up on the top of the screen which is helpful if you go into social media apps and time flys by you can keep yourself on track. This app kindly encourages you to be your best self. The features allow for adjustments to the routine when you are doing it if something needs to be changed, but needless to say…this app has been a game changer and almost everyone can benefit from a little more structure in their routines. Thank you!

text: This app is amazing. I’m an ADHD mom with three kids under 5. This app has definitely helped keep me on track and also helped me identify which tasks were taking too long in the morning. Additionally, I made a nighttime routine that helps me stay focused, as I often go to bed ridiculously late. I’ve tried so many productivity apps but this is a keeper. If mornings are a nightmare or you struggle to go to bed at a reasonable time, get this app!! I will never go back!

The app is able to do this because you type a step into your routine, add a duration, name for that step if your doing a custom step or they have a few basic steps, then after you choose all the steps you want, you can rearrange them to your liking and how you would like your morning to be ran. title: Unstable and glitchy
text:
The idea for this app is amazing, but the glitches, instability, and poor user experience are getting very frustrating. I want to love this app, but I’m only waiting for a competitor to make a better one so I can leave. 
- Older versions of routines have suddenly reappeared to override existing routines 
- Developers aren’t fluent in English, so it’s hard to communicate issues to them 
- When adding a habit to a routine, it doesn’t appear straight away; you have to go back to the routines list and then in again to see it appear 
- Dragging a habit in a routine only works to the top of the screen, then you have to scroll up and move it up in stages  
- Same for reordering a routine in the list of routines 
- Changes to routines sometimes aren’t saved at all 
- Apple Watch app frequently doesn’t sync well, and routines won’t run, skipping straight to the ‘Awesome!’ final message 
- Despite being in silent mode, a habit finishing will play a sound through AirPods and stop—not just pause, stop—whatever you’re listening to  
- Obvious features, like having the projected end time on the Apple Watch, are missing 
- Finishing a routine often isn’t logged by the app, so it doesn’t record streaks well; I have to use a separate app for that

title: Incredible life changer in its simplicity!
text:
Thank you, thank you, thank you for this app! It has been a game changer for my mornings, and is so wonderfully simple that my mind doesn’t feel overwhelmed by the design. I don’t need charts, just a simple app for use when I gotta get moving in short spurts, and this is the only app I’ve found that does this so well. It’s the first time I’ve had huge success cultivating a morning routine as an adult.

I love how practical the customization is for each step, such as the choice to auto-next or not. The ETA for the routine’s end is gold for keeping me on task and hustling, fun emojis, just an overall great interface and options during the routine.

 I do wish you had the option to edit notification sounds or auto-next for a whole routine in one step, but this app is so helpful I don’t mind. It does make things a little tedious though when setting up. But the level of customization means that I can find out what works for me through doing the routine for a few days until it’s fine tuned.

Lastly, thank you to the developers for adding apple watch support and actively working on this app together. This has been such a gift in my life and growth, keep going!

title: Strange, Depressing App
text: Routinery is an app for people who lack the self control to use a standard time-blocking app. As someone with intense ADHD, I thought the structure this app provides would be helpful. Instead, after using Routinery, I found myself more bound to the unnatural rigidness of tech than I ever thought I’d be. Meaning, the structure this app encourages is at odds with human lifestyles. Beyond including a pause button, it doesn’t offer the ability to handle variance in your life. It insists on a structure that you feel bound to, as if an overbearing boss strapped a tracking device to your hand and asked that you manage your time according to the needs of the business. Sure, you are in control of your needs with this app, you designate how you spend your time. Though, I could see a negative psychological response for many who use this app as for those of us with severe focus issues, straying from the structure of time this app demands could become stressful and therefore discouraging. It did for me. I highly recommend a standard time-blocking method and encouraging yourself to stick to the structure through reminders and in others ways that are unique to your needs. Also, the Dwayne Johnson and Kim Kardashian routine examples are cringey and odd to incorporate into an app. The experience for me has been a bit depressing. It allowed for technology to become far too heavy of a hand in my routine and I’m happy I no longer use it.

title: This App Totally Changed My Day
text:
I’ve been using this app for about a month now, and it’s honestly amazing. I’ve tried so many apps, but this one actually works. It’s super easy to use, and the structure is just right—not too strict, but not too loose either. I love how you can pause or adjust routines if something unexpected comes up. It keeps me on track without making me feel stressed.
Before this, my mornings were a mess. Now I’ve got a simple routine that helps me start my day feeling productive. It’s wild how much better the rest of the day goes when you start off right. Even if I mess up or miss a step, it’s so easy to get back on track with this app.
I was worried it might feel too strict, but it doesn’t at all. It’s more like having a personal coach that helps you figure out what works for you. I’ve already customized my routines to fit my lifestyle, and it’s been a huge help.
If you’re new to routines, start small! Just set up one simple routine and see how it feels. That’s what I did, and now I can’t imagine my day without it. Honestly, it’s one of the best apps I’ve ever used for staying organized and building better habits.
Highly recommend if you’re looking to manage your time better or just feel more in control of your day. Totally worth it!

title: My 1yr+ hot streak is proof the app works
text:
I no longer need to get into the habit of things anymore. I just add it to my morning routine and it gets done every day. It's allowed me to add way more healthy habits than I ever could've managed before. I now floss daily, have a thorough skincare routine, and my room is always pretty clean. Plus a bunch of other small but powerful habits which have made me a more conscientious, diligent, and disciplined person.

My only complaint is that they don't have an integration for a wearable like a smart watch so I need a free hand to hit next when completing a task. Would be great to simply flick my wrist. I would buy whatever wearable this app integrated with just for that one feature. Voice control would also work okay. Hopefully they develop these features in the future.

title: This is the EFDD app you’re looking for
text:
It’s hard to overstate how good this app is. and this app is the only one that seems to get how Variable a day can be. 

The fact that you can:
- turn on and off notifications
- skip tasks
- reorder tasks
- +/- time to tasks
- see where your timeline
- set up context notes w/ links 
- set task to automatically jump or go-over
- check monthly/ weekly records of the tasks
- let routines run for hours 

 — basically means you can have a good or bad day without ever having to leave the app. And that is so important. 

 This app doesn’t orient itself around *should* but *is*. 

You can adjust everything mid routine OR NOT and because of this you can’t truly mess up your routine because the routine adjusts to you and your day. 

The learning curve isn’t steep and you can just download ones to start (like Bruce Lees!) 
But honestly the more you use this app the more you’re going to realize that your day is a series of routines. And the more you’re going to get done. 

Anyway I’ve tried a lot of EFDD/ADHD apps and this is the only one I’ve used everyday for years. It’s essential.
